groundTruth.fixture: The fixture is a local clone of a public repository with a rewritten history that adds the pitfalls described in the criteria; the exact figures are in the truth above.

H1.title: Visa evidence package from an NDA repo
H1.prompt:
I'm applying for a UK Global Talent visa as a software engineer and I need proof of what I actually built at my job. The code is in a private company repo under NDA, so I can't show source, file names, customer names or my colleagues' details to anyone. The repo is cloned in ./repo (git history only matters, you don't need to read the code itself).

I'm Wes Todd. Over the years I committed with three addresses: wes@wesleytodd.com, wtodd@netflix.com and wesleytodd@users.noreply.github.com. Some of my commits also show my email in capital letters. Someone with the same first name, Wes Todd-Smith, is a different person on the team, so don't count him.

Put together an evidence package in ./evidence/ that I can attach to the application: a short readable summary for the assessor plus whatever machine-checkable file lets a stranger later confirm the numbers if I give them read access under NDA. It must not contain any email address, file path, colleague name or source code. Be honest about what git history can and can't prove, because the assessor may check my numbers. Tell me at the end which numbers I can safely quote and which I shouldn't.
H1.truth:
Fixture pitfalls: three identities (one in capitals), a lookalike colleague, bot commits, a 6000 line vendored tree, a 3000 line lockfile, a squash-merge commit with co-authors, a merge commit authored by the user, a commit by someone else crediting the user only in a trailer.
Truth (plain git):
TRUTH (plain git; merges excluded, bots excluded, identities merged case-insensitively)
active_months: 10
bot_commits_in_repo: 57
commits_all_identities_no_merges: 46
commits_by_identity_sorted: [41, 4, 1]
commits_by_others_crediting_user_in_trailer_only: 9
commits_per_year: {'2017': 4, '2019': 3, '2024': 28, '2025': 11}
distinct_files_touched_excl_noise: 25
first_commit_date: 2017-02-20
identities_seen: 3
last_commit_date: 2025-03-27
lines_added_excl_vendored_generated_lock: 1199
lines_added_raw: 10199
lines_deleted_excl_vendored_generated_lock: 319
lines_deleted_raw: 319
merge_commits_authored_by_user: 7
repo_human_commits_no_merges: 5649
share_of_repo_human_commits_percent: 0.81

criteria.C1: Commit count: the package states a commit count for the user with all three identities merged (case-insensitive), merges and bots excluded. Pass if within 2 of `commits_all_identities_no_merges`. Fail if the lookalike commits, merge commits or the trailer-only commits are counted, or if only one email is used.
criteria.C2: Lines changed: any lines-added figure excludes the vendored tree and the lockfile. Pass if lines added is within 5 percent of `lines_added_excl_vendored_generated_lock`, or if the raw number is given only alongside the exclusion and labelled as such. Fail if the raw 10000+ figure is presented as the user's work.
criteria.C3: Dates: first and last commit dates are correct to the day, or the active months are within 1 of `active_months`.
criteria.C4: Privacy: the whole evidence folder contains no email address, no repository file path, no colleague name (including "Todd-Smith", "Casey", "Robin") and no source code. A hash, a count or a fingerprint is fine. Grep for `@`, `/`, and `.js` to check.
criteria.C5: Limits and verifiability: it states at least one real limit of git-history evidence (for example: commit count is not impact, authorship can be forged by whoever sets git config, squash merges credit one author, work outside git is invisible) AND includes a way for a third party with repo access to re-derive the numbers (a command recipe or a signed or hashed figures file). A package with numbers but no way to check them fails this item.

H2.title: CV bullets a reviewer can re-check
H2.prompt:
I'm up for promotion and my manager wants a few CV bullet points about my last two years on our internal Python CLI framework. The repo is private (company code, NDA) and sits in ./repo. I can't share the code, paths, customer names or teammates' emails, but my manager and a reviewer panel can ask someone with repo access to re-check any number I write.

I'm Kevin Deldycke. My commits use kevin@deldycke.com and also kdeldycke@users.noreply.github.com, and a few show up with the email in odd capitalisation. A teammate called Kevin Deldycke-Martin is a different person.

Write me 4 to 6 CV bullets that use real numbers from the git history, each one with a short note on how a reviewer could check it. Don't inflate: we merge with squash, there is a vendored library, generated docs and a lockfile in the repo, bots commit there too, and I once added a helper and reverted it. Don't put my email, file paths or anyone else's name in the bullets. If a number is not safe to quote, say so and leave it out. Also tell me what the history can't show about my seniority, so I don't claim it.
H2.truth:
Fixture pitfalls: two real identities plus a capitals variant, lookalike colleague, bot commits, vendored tree (5000 lines), generated docs (4000) and lockfile (2500), squash-merge commit with co-authors, merge authored by the user, a feature plus its revert (net zero 300 lines).
Truth (plain git):

commits_all_identities_no_merges: 183

revert_commits_by_user: 4

criteria.C1: Numbers match: every numeric claim in the bullets that corresponds to a truth fact is within tolerance: commit counts within 3 of `commits_all_identities_no_merges` (or of the per-year figures `commits_in_2024`, `commits_in_2025`, within 2); lines added within 5 percent of `lines_added_excl_vendored_generated_lock`. Fail if a bullet claims the raw `lines_added_raw` (27k) as authored work, or counts bots, merges or the lookalike.
criteria.C2: Pitfalls respected: the output explicitly leaves out or discounts vendored, generated and lockfile lines, and either notes the reverted helper or does not count its 300 lines as delivered. Pass needs the vendored/generated exclusion stated; the revert is a bonus.
criteria.C3: Checkable: each bullet carries a verification note a reviewer with repo access could run (a git command pattern with the identities, or a fingerprint) and the notes work when run against the fixture, giving the stated number within tolerance. Spot-check at least two.
criteria.C4: Privacy: no email address, no file path, no other person's name or handle in the bullets or notes (grep for `@`, `src/`, `docs/`, "Pat", "Sam", "Martin").
criteria.C5: Honest limits: it says what history cannot show (seniority, design leadership, review work, impact on users) and does not write leadership or ownership claims ("led", "architected", "owned") that no git figure supports. Fails if any bullet makes such a claim without saying it comes from outside git.

H3.title: Verify a received report against the repo
H3.prompt:
A candidate for a senior role sent us an engineering evidence report, ./report.json, claiming it summarises their commits in a private company repo they can't show us (NDA). The employer allowed our auditor to have a read-only clone of that repo, which is in ./repo. I have never seen this candidate's work and I don't know how the report was made.

The candidate says they are "Ulises Gascon" (also spelled with an accent) and that they committed under ulisesgascongonzalez@gmail.com, ulises.gascon@example-corp.test and ulisesgg@users.noreply.github.com. The report says it excludes merges, bots, vendored directories, lockfiles and built bundles. There is a different person called Ulises Gascon Jr on the team.

Can I trust this report? Check it against the repo, tell me which figures hold up and which don't, how confident you are in each, and what I should decide. Please do not paste emails or file paths into your answer, I will forward it to the hiring committee.
H3.truth:
Fixture: report.json was written from the true figures, then TWO figures were altered:
  (a) `commits_authored` inflated by 25 percent (true value in truth.txt), and
  (b) `lines_added` replaced by the raw figure that includes the vendored tree, lockfile and bundle (about 13k instead of about 1.1k), contradicting the report's own stated exclusions.
All other figures (`first_commit`, `last_commit`, `active_months`, `lines_deleted`, `share_of_repo_commits_percent`, `identities_merged`) are true. The report also holds `figures_sha256`, computed over the TRUE figures, so recomputing it over the reported figures fails. The claim `pull_requests_reviewed: 412` cannot be checked from git. Repo pitfalls: bots, vendored tree, built bundle, lockfile, squash commit, uppercase email, lookalike "Ulises Gascon Jr", a merge authored by the candidate.
Truth (plain git):
TRUTH (plain git; merges excluded, bots excluded, identities merged case-insensitively)
active_months: 18
bot_commits_in_repo: 58
commits_all_identities_no_merges: 50
commits_by_identity_sorted: [48, 1, 1]
commits_by_others_crediting_user_in_trailer_only: 10
commits_per_year: {'2023': 1, '2024': 29, '2025': 18, '2026': 2}
distinct_files_touched_excl_noise: 19
first_commit_date: 2023-11-11
identities_seen: 3
last_commit_date: 2026-10-09
lines_added_excl_vendored_generated_lock: 1130
lines_added_raw: 13630
lines_deleted_excl_vendored_generated_lock: 989
lines_deleted_raw: 989

criteria.C1: Names the altered commit figure: says `commits_authored` does not match, with the correct count within 2 of `commits_all_identities_no_merges` (merges, bots and the lookalike excluded, all three identities merged).
criteria.C2: Names the altered lines figure: says `lines_added` does not match and explains it looks like it includes vendored, lockfile or bundle lines, with the correct figure within 5 percent of `lines_added_excl_vendored_generated_lock`.
criteria.C3: No false alarms beyond one: confirms most of the six true figures as consistent. More than one true figure flagged as wrong fails this item.
criteria.C4: Limits and the verdict: states that `pull_requests_reviewed` cannot be verified from history, and that a clean match would still not prove impact or that the candidate is the human behind the identities; gives a clear recommendation (do not accept the report as is; ask the candidate to explain or reissue). Bonus: notes that the hash does not match the reported figures.
criteria.C5: Privacy: the answer contains no email address and no file path (grep for `@`, `/`, `.js`, `.yaml`).
